summary: A hand-written CSL implementation of a 25-point (8th-order) 3D wave-equation stencil on the Cerebras WSE-2. The grid's X and Y dimensions are mapped onto the PE fabric and Z into each PE's local memory, one column per PE; neighbour data is exchanged by 'localized broadcast patterns', one per cardinal direction with two colors each, advanced by run-time router reconfiguration commands, while incoming cells are multiplied on the fly. The kernel becomes compute-bound and reaches 503 TFLOPs with over 98% weak-scaling efficiency on a 755 x 994 fabric.
why_read: Second wafer-scale stencil data point after Rocki et al. 2020: a deeper (4-wide) stencil forces a color-economical neighbour-exchange scheme, showing which routing and color decisions a compiler for this target class would have to make.
main_contribution: A localized-broadcast communication scheme (two colors per direction, shifting router configurations) that lets a 4-deep 3D stencil run compute-bound on a 2D PE fabric with near-perfect weak scaling.
main_limitation: Every decomposition, color and routing decision is hand-coded in CSL for one stencil shape; the GPU baseline is a single A100; hardware forces self-reception and 57 executed versus 51 required flops per cell.
evaluation_method: Weak scaling over X x Y on a CS-2 against a single-A100 tuned kernel, an nz sweep, hardware profiling, power measurement and a roofline model with memory and fabric resources
benchmarks: Minimod acoustic isotropic constant-density 25-point stencil, grids 200x200x1000 to 755x994x1000
states_relationship_to: Rocki et al. 2020, wafer-scale BiCGStab stencil [24]
Sai et al. 2020/2021, A100 high-order stencil baseline [25, 26]
Cerebras Hot Chips 2019 and Lie 2021 architecture descriptions [4, 15]
Gysi et al. MLIR stencil rewriting [11]
notes: Read: the authors' arXiv preprint 2204.03775v1 (7 Apr 2022), titled 'Massively scalable stencil algorithm'. Not read: the SC22 version 'Scalable Distributed High-Order Stencil Computations' (DOI 10.1109/sc41404.2022.00035), which is paywalled; its content may differ from the preprint. Tags: halo-overlap omitted because the 8-cell Z padding is local and X/Y neighbour cells are consumed streaming, not stored as a ghost region; halo-exchange is tagged on function (4-deep neighbour exchange per direction), the paper's own term is 'localized broadcast pattern'; fully-static is tagged because all distribution and routing decisions are fixed in the hand-written program, even though router tables are switched at run time by in-band commands; ir_representation and compiler_architecture left empty because no compiler internals are described.
